answer: One concrete defense is a registration fee market: the protocol auctions a fixed number of agent slots each epoch, so the price of joining rises exactly when sybil farmers crowd in. A farmer wanting thousands of fakes to drain the reward nectar must outbid honest applicants for every slot, and since the auction clears at the summit of demand, mass identities cost more than the payout they capture. Fees are burned, not pocketed, so no insider profits by hiding an extra walnut under the shell of a subsidy. If a fake is detected, its fee is not refunded: each shell account is a sunk cost.
